item.title: Kenyan fresh-cut flowers blossom in Chinese market
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
People talk in front of a rose wall at the Kenya Pavilion during the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) on Nov. 7, 2026. At the Kenya Pavilion during the ninth CIIE, a rose wall over two meters high has drawn many visitors to stop and take photos. Kenya hopes to use this year's expo as a platform to bring the fragrance of Kenyan flowers into the Chinese market. Thanks to favorable natural conditions, Kenyan fresh-cut flowers are prized for their consistent quality and stable production, and the country has long ranked first in Africa in flower exports. Kenya is among the 53 African countries harvesting the early fruits of China's zero-tariff policy, which came into force on May 1. This has made it easier for African specialty agricultural products to enter China and boosted the confidence of Kenyan flower growers in exporting to the Chinese market. From the East African highlands to the Chinese market, the journey is getting shorter, the connections are growing closer, and the direction is becoming clearer. Kenyan fresh-cut flowers are now enjoying a golden age in China. item.title: How AI is rewriting China's TV playbook
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
by Xinhua writers Zhang Yunlong and Bai Ying BEIJING, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- A 30-episode mythological drama with a live-action look can now be produced in just months using artificial intelligence (AI), compared with the years conventional production methods would require. Made entirely with AI-generated imagery and performances, the TV series "Beyond Wukong," China's first AI-generated long-form drama, offers a glimpse into a broader transformation in China's TV industry. AI is evolving from an auxiliary tool into a core driver of production, according to a recent industry report. The 2026 China TV drama (online drama) development report, released by the National Radio and Television Administration, identifies six major trends in the sector, including changes in production structures, creative approaches, technology, business models, institutional support and international distribution. AI is increasingly being applied at multiple stages of production, rather than being used solely to create standalone AI-generated works, the report says. At the script-development stage, AI can assist with script generation and creative development. During pre-production and production, it can help with location scouting and reduce costs associated with background performers. In post-production, applications include rough-cut editing, noise reduction, color correction, image restoration, and correction of visual errors. Major streaming platforms are also developing tools to support AI-assisted production. iQIYI's NadouPro platform, launched in April, has attracted more than 20,000 active creators and supported over 100 film and television projects within two months, according to the report. Tencent Video expanded its WorkRally platform in June, with new versions for professional film and television production and high-quality animation, extending its capabilities to the full production process for live-action dramas and animated works. Mango TV's Lumecreate platform integrates more than 40 image and video generation models and over 80 functions. "Beyond Wukong" shows how Lumecreate can support long-form drama production. Adapted from "Later Journey to the West," a novel written during the Ming and Qing dynasties as a sequel to the classic "Journey to the West," the drama follows Sun Xiaosheng, a young stone-born monkey, as he investigates the mysterious petrification of Mount Huaguo's elders before joining a monk and his disciples on a new journey westward. The series premiered on Mango TV at 6 p.m. on Aug. 31 this year, before airing at 8 p.m. in a prime-time drama slot on Hunan Satellite TV, with each episode running about 40 minutes. According to Hunan Satellite TV, the series ranked first in real-time ratings among provincial satellite channels during its time slot on the debut day. So far, 10 of the planned 30 episodes have been released, with the rest scheduled for release this winter. Ren Xu, general manager of Mango TV's AIGC innovation content center, said the series' production cost was about one-eighth to one-tenth that of a comparable S-level (top-tier) live-action drama of the same genre. But the process was not simply about generating images automatically. "Humans lead. AI executes," Ren told Xinhua in an interview. Directors, screenwriters and art professionals remained involved throughout production, checking visual quality and correcting artificial-looking images and other distortions by adjusting art direction and algorithms. Ren said Lumecreate had largely addressed the challenge of maintaining visual consistency. For "Beyond Wukong," the team built 340 character assets and 285 scene assets, standardizing character designs and scene styles in the system for reuse in the remaining episodes and a potential second season. Emotional and performance continuity, however, remains more difficult, as current AI systems still struggle to interpret complex subtext and subtle emotional shifts. To address this, the team broke down longer shots into shorter segments, with directors and art professionals providing precise instructions on the emotions to be conveyed. Editors ensured the sequences flowed smoothly and logically. "Technology solves the problem of visual consistency, while our creators are responsible for ensuring convincing performances and narrative coherence," Ren said. AI is also reshaping production teams and the skills they need. Ren said AI had sharply reduced demand for some traditional hands-on production roles, such as set construction, lighting and camera operation, while creating new roles, such as AI directors and AIGC coordinators. "Creators increasingly need to understand AI tools and technical processes alongside their established skills," she said. Mango TV has organized multiple hands-on AI training sessions across the company, and employees have signed up enthusiastically. In an article published on the WeChat account of the China Press Publication Radio and Television Journal, Yang Weiran, deputy head of the art committee at Xiaoxiang Pictures, said the series had demonstrated the commercial viability of AI-generated long-form content on mainstream screens, citing its audience ratings, online buzz and positive capital market response. However, AI adoption is not uniform across the film and TV industries. Speaking to Xinhua at a special screening of "Three Kingdoms: The Beginning" in July, Yu Zhou, president of animation studio Light Chaser Animation, said the studio had not used AI-generated imagery in the animated feature. The AI-assisted tools available at the time had not yet met the studio's expectations for consistent output quality, Yu said, adding that his studio remained open to adopting the technology once it met its standards. While some studios remain cautious, AI is also being tested in theatrical film production. "Sanxingdui: Future Past," billed as China's first AI-generated theatrical feature, opened on Oct. 23. Set in a future where a super-AI system triggers a global catastrophe, the film follows an archaeologist who discovers that inscriptions on Sanxingdui bronzes may hold the key to averting the crisis. The film had grossed just 1.79 million yuan (about 266,000 U.S. dollars) as of Monday, according to ticketing platform Maoyan. Chen Xuguang, director of Peking University's Institute of Film, Television and Theater, said it featured grand visuals, had a strong audiovisual impact and showed considerable imagination, although its performances lacked subtlety. "Regardless of its box office performance," he added, "the film deserved recognition for being a pioneer." These developments point to a broader challenge for the screen industry: AI's ability to generate long-form audiovisual content does not necessarily translate into compelling storytelling, consistent visual quality or sustained audience engagement. AI can accelerate production and reduce costs, but the quality of the finished work still depends on human creative judgment. ■

item.title: CIIE Voices: What keeps global businesses coming back?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
Why do global businesses keep coming back to the China International Import Expo (CIIE)? And what makes the Chinese market so vital to their long-term strategies? Global companies, including Intel, Philips, and IQAir, share their perspectives at this year's CIIE. Their answers go beyond market size, they highlight China's fast-evolving innovation ecosystem, digital transformation, expanding opportunities and the value of partnering with local players.

item.title: China rejects spy allegation linked to Nvidia CEO
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
BEIJING, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun on Monday rejected an allegation of Chinese spying following media reports that Nvidia had opened a probe into its CEO Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with a woman U.S. officials say was working for Chinese intelligence. "The so-called Chinese spy allegation is groundless. It is nothing but a smear against China," Guo said at a regular news briefing when asked to comment on the reports. ■

item.title: Economic Watch: China's consumer prices maintain mild recovery in October
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
BEIJING, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- China's consumer inflation remained mild in October, with the consumer price index (CPI) rising 0.7 percent year on year, while factory-gate prices increased at a faster pace, official data showed Monday. Month on month, the CPI was flat, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). In the first 10 months of 2026, consumer prices rose 0.9 percent from a year earlier. The year-on-year increase in October was mainly driven by non-food prices, which rose 1.5 percent, while food prices fell 2.9 percent, weighing on overall inflation. Food, tobacco, alcohol and dining out prices declined 1.6 percent year on year, dragging down the CPI by 0.48 percentage points. Fresh vegetable prices dropped 16.9 percent, pork prices fell 8.6 percent, and fresh fruit prices declined 3.8 percent, while egg prices rose 12.3 percent. Among the other seven categories, six saw year-on-year price increases and one declined. Transportation and communication prices led the gains with a 5.5 percent increase, followed by health care at 2.4 percent and other supplies and services at 1.8 percent. Housing-related costs fell 0.3 percent. On a monthly basis, food, tobacco, alcohol and dining out prices fell 0.5 percent, dragging down the CPI by 0.16 percentage points. Transportation and communication, education, culture and recreation, and health care prices rose 1.0 percent, 0.3 percent and 0.1 percent, respectively. NBS statistician Dong Lijuan attributed the price movements to a combination of imported inflation and domestic demand. Gasoline prices surged 22.4 percent year on year, accelerating 5.8 percentage points from September and contributing about 0.63 percentage points to the CPI increase. Prices of data storage equipment, tablet computers, computers and mobile phones rose 45.4 percent, 29.3 percent, 23 percent and 16.7 percent, respectively, together adding about 0.26 percentage points, reflecting robust demand in artificial intelligence and computing-related sectors. Wang Guanhua, NBS spokesperson, said that, while global inflationary pressure has mounted significantly and major economies have seen sharp price increases, China's price gains remain relatively mild. He attributed this to the country's complete industrial system, reliable industrial and supply chains, early development of a new energy system, market diversification strategy and timely and effective price-stabilizing policies. China's producer price index (PPI) rose 5.7 percent year on year in October, up from a 5 percent increase in September. Month on month, PPI rose 0.7 percent, with the pace of increase narrowing 0.5 percentage points from September. The PPI growth was led by energy-related sectors. Coal mining and washing prices jumped 36.6 percent year on year, while oil and natural gas extraction prices rose 35 percent. Downstream refined petroleum product manufacturing, organic chemical raw material manufacturing, coal processing, and gas production and supply posted monthly increases of 6.8 percent, 6.8 percent, 3.2 percent and 1.5 percent, respectively. Orderly capacity adjustment and artificial intelligence development also pushed up some industrial prices, with non-metallic mineral products rising 0.8 percent month on month, automobile manufacturing flattening after three months of declines, and electrical machinery and computer electronics edging up 0.1 percent. Liu Fang, a researcher with the National Development and Reform Commission, said the mild price recovery has helped improve corporate profitability, with profits of large industrial firms rising 15.5 percent in the first nine months. As policies aimed at stabilizing growth, expanding domestic demand and supporting businesses are further implemented, prices are expected to continue a mild upward trend, Liu added. ■

item.title: Xi congratulates Iotova on election as Bulgarian president
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
BEIJING, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has extended congratulations to Iliana Iotova on her election as president of Bulgaria. In a message on Friday, Xi noted that Bulgaria was the second country in the world to establish diplomatic ties with the People's Republic of China, and that mutual respect, equality, and mutual benefit and win-win results have been hallmarks of the bilateral relations. In recent years, the two countries have been steadily advancing exchanges and cooperation at all levels and across all fields, while their strategic partnership has continued to deepen, said Xi. Xi also said that he attaches great importance to the development of the China-Bulgaria ties. He pledged to work with Iotova to guide the two countries as they march together along their respective paths to development and revitalization, build an even more positive, practical and dynamic bilateral relationship, and thereby bring greater benefits to the two peoples. ■

item.title: How Xi steers China's green transformation and global climate action
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-09
BEIJING, Nov. 9 (Xinhua) -- In 2026, the intensifying fallout of global climate change -- manifesting in catastrophic flooding, rampant wildfires, and record heatwaves -- reaffirms the imperative for immediate, coordinated global action. With global climate tipping points looming, the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), set to kick off on Monday in Antalya, Türkiye, will offer a new opportunity for the international community to renew momentum for more effective global climate cooperation. Under the leadership of President Xi Jinping, China has over the years stayed committed to advancing ecological protection and green transition domestically, and promoting international climate cooperation, making major global contributions to the world's fight against what many regard as an existential threat to humanity. "LIKE WE PROTECT OUR EYES" "We should protect the environment like we protect our eyes." This evocative principle -- voiced on various occasions by Xi -- frames ecological conservation not merely as a policy choice, but as a vital imperative drawn directly from his own experiences. "Over four decades ago, I lived and worked for many years in a small village on the Loess Plateau in western China," Xi recalled in reply to a letter from student representatives of the Global Alliance of Universities on Climate in 2020. Back then, the ecology and environment there was seriously damaged due to over-development, and the local people were trapped in poverty as a result. That experience has taught him that man and nature are a community of life and that the damage done to nature will ultimately hurt humanity. An avid reader of Chinese classics, Xi has also been deeply influenced by the traditional Chinese philosophy that views man as an integral part of nature. "All beings flourish when they live in harmony and receive nourishment from nature," he has said. This conviction underpins the signature environmental doctrine that "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets," which Xi first introduced in 2005 while serving as Party chief of east China's Zhejiang Province. Upon becoming General Secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee in 2012, Xi made ecological conservation a national priority. For Xi, ecological conservation requires not only a profound shift in development philosophy, but also robust institutional safeguards. As he has put it, "Eco-environmental protection relies on laws and regulations." At his direction, environmental performance has become a key criterion for evaluating officials, while environmental inspections have reinforced local governments' accountability for fulfilling their environmental responsibilities. Together, these measures have helped steer China's economic growth toward a more resource-efficient and sustainable path. Since 2012, China has sustained a 6 percent average annual economic growth rate while capping an average energy consumption increase to just 3.3 percent. This structural decoupling yielded a 26.1 percent cumulative decline in energy intensity, marking one of the steepest efficiency gains globally. Xi has also led by example in promoting environmental protection and green development. Since becoming China's top leader, he has personally participated in tree-planting activities in Beijing for 14 consecutive years. Forests have the capacity to conserve water, bring in economic benefits, and boost grain production, and now serve well as a carbon sink, he has noted. Today, China has expanded its forest coverage to over 25 percent of its land area, planting trees across an area roughly 1.7 times the size of California since 2012. The annual carbon-sink capacity of China's forests and grassland has exceeded 1.2 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalents. Fuad Gani, vice director of the Graduate School of Sustainable Development at the University of Indonesia, said that China's ecological conservation philosophy stands out for its ability to translate environmental goals into long-term policies and governance frameworks. "It is one of China's most valuable contributions to advancing green transformation on the global stage," he said. "SOMETHING WE MUST DO OURSELVES" Balancing economic growth with green development remains a challenge for economies worldwide, especially emerging markets seeking to meet development needs while pursuing environmental sustainability. In Xi's view, economic growth and the green transition are not opposing forces, but complementary goals. This philosophy is captured in his defining doctrine -- "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets." Achieving China's carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, Xi has stressed, "is not something that others ask us to do, but something we must do ourselves." Under his leadership, China has effectively aligned emissions reduction with technological innovation, industrial upgrading and energy security, turning the green transition into an increasingly important driver of high-quality development. As early as 2014, when conventional gasoline-powered vehicles still dominated China's roads, Xi recognized the enormous potential of new energy vehicles (NEVs). During an inspection tour of SAIC Motor, a major Chinese carmaker, Xi depicted developing NEVs as the only way for China to move from a major automobile country to an automobile powerhouse. In the following decade, the president has demonstrated consistent support for electric cars, visiting automotive companies, touring laboratories, and showing great interest in trying new home-developed models. China's NEV industry has since grown rapidly, emerging as a flagship of the country's technology-intensive manufacturing sector. Beyond the NEV sector, China has also built the world's largest and most comprehensive clean energy industrial chain, with green and low-carbon industries emerging as an important engine of economic growth. The growing exports of the "new three" -- photovoltaic products, lithium-ion batteries and electric vehicles -- are a testament to China's successful shift toward innovation-driven manufacturing. Beyond its own borders, China is now channeling this green innovation momentum into regional cooperation. China will continue to work with fellow Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) countries to increase the installed capacity of photovoltaic and wind power each by 10 million kilowatts, and nurture more green industry talents through China-SCO cooperation, said Xi at the 26th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the SCO this September. China's exports of solar panels, wind turbines, electric vehicles and batteries this year will help the world to avoid 450 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions, according to a recent analysis by the Finland-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air. The development exemplifies China's strategic push to cultivate "new quality productive forces" -- a policy concept first articulated by Xi in 2023 to drive high-tech innovation and sustainable economic modernization. "Green development," as Xi once put it, "is the defining feature of high-quality development, and new quality productive forces are green in nature." China has turned the challenges of addressing climate change into opportunities for technological innovation, industrial upgrading and high-quality economic development, said Wang Lei, a professor at the School of Government of Beijing Normal University. "Guided by the goals of reducing carbon emissions and strengthening climate resilience, the country has leveraged policy guidance, market incentives and open innovation to drive the transformation of energy, industry, transportation and construction," he added. "EXTREME RESOLUTIONS" Deeply committed to joining world nations to build a community with a shared future for humanity, Xi has repeatedly called on the international community to strengthen cooperation in addressing climate change and actively advanced the building of a fair and equitable global climate governance system for win-win cooperation. "Supreme resources spring from extreme resolutions," Xi said, invoking a perceptive line from French writer Victor Hugo's Les Miserables during his address to the historic 2015 Paris climate change conference. During the summit, Xi put forward important ideas and proposals and worked actively to build consensus among parties, making an indispensable contribution to the eventual adoption of the Paris Agreement. At a special ceremony on Sept. 3, 2016, Xi solemnly handed over China's instrument of joining the Paris Agreement to then UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon. "Had not been President Xi Jinping's initiative, we would not have the Paris Agreement on climate change even now," Ban said in a 2021 interview with Xinhua. In response to the grave challenge of climate change, China has taken on its international responsibilities with what Xi described as "extreme resolutions." At a virtual UN gathering in 2020, Xi announced that China would strive to peak carbon dioxide emissions before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality before 2060. In 2021, he pledged that China would not build new coal-fired power projects abroad. In recent years, some developed countries, particularly those in the West, have backtracked on their climate commitments, undermining global climate governance. Against this backdrop, Xi announced China's 2035 Nationally Determined Contributions in 2025, including a commitment to reduce economy-wide net greenhouse gas emissions by 7-10 percent from peak levels and to raise the share of non-fossil fuels in total energy consumption to more than 30 percent by 2035. For the first time, China committed to absolute emissions reduction targets covering all economic sectors and all greenhouse gases, providing much-needed certainty and stability for global climate governance. Xi has also emphasized the need to uphold fairness and equity and fully respect developing countries' right to development as the world pursues a green transition. "The transition should serve to narrow rather than widen the North-South gap," he said, urging developed countries to take the lead in fulfilling emissions reduction obligations and provide more financial and technological support to developing countries. Under Xi's leadership, China has been striving to strengthen South-South cooperation on climate change. Xi has proposed the establishment of the Belt and Road Initiative International Green Development Coalition and advocated building a green BRICS partnership. Through these target-driven initiatives, China seeks to deepen cooperation in clean energy, green technology and green industrial development, while helping developing countries strengthen their capacity to address climate change. "The Earth is our one and only home," Xi has said. "To scale up efforts to address climate change and promote sustainable development bears on the future of humanity."■

item.title: Xi votes in local legislative election in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, casts his ballot to elect deputies to the Xicheng district people's congress at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Xicheng District of Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping cast his ballot at a polling station in Beijing on Friday to elect deputies to a local people's congress. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, voted at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Xicheng District to elect deputies to the Xicheng district people's congress. Xi stressed efforts to practice whole-process people's democracy, uphold Party leadership, and strengthen oversight throughout the election process to ensure that deputies who meet the people's expectations are elected. Around 3:30 p.m. Friday, Xi arrived at the polling station, gave his voter registration card to staff for verification, and got a ballot. He cast his ballot after filling it. Noting that the election of deputies to people's congresses is an important foundation for upholding, improving and practicing the people's congress system, Xi underlined the need to give full play to democracy, strictly act in accordance with the law, and ensure that the election is carried out fairly and cleanly. On Friday afternoon, other senior Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi cast their ballots in person, while Han Zheng entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Former Chinese leader Hu Jintao also entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Friday saw people vote at 13,054 polling stations across Beijing to elect 4,898 new deputies to the people's congresses at the district level and 11,137 deputies to the township-level people's congresses. ■ Chinese Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, casts his ballot to elect deputies to a local people's congress at the Ziguangge polling station of the Wenjin Street electoral district in Xicheng District of Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026.
